findings.claim: A rename, move or copy of a subtitle-serving row that has no own sidecars skips the owner-change check. A sidecar-less video renamed or moved onto a longer stem silently takes another video's sidecar.
findings.impact: Example: renaming clip.mp4 to movie.ja.mp4 in a folder holding movie.mp4 and movie.ja.srt answers 200. movie.mp4 silently loses its Japanese track, and movie.ja.mp4 now plays it as its default track. The same happens when a sidecar-less movie.ja.mp4 is moved, or copied, into such a folder. Upload init refuses the same arrival.
findings.evidence: In backend/app/services/fileops.py:493-495 `_sidecar_carry_plan` returns `[]` when `own` is empty, before plan_sidecar_carry runs its dest_index.all() owner-change loop. In fileops.py:1216-1218 batch rename does `if not own: continue`, which also skips sim.apply, so later steps see stale stems. In fileops.py:333-342 copy_file uses the sidecar-aware candidate check only when `own` is non-empty. By contrast, upload.py init_upload calls arrival_owner_changes unconditionally. No test covers a sidecar-less mover.
findings.repro: Reasoned from the code, not run: seed movie.mp4 and clip.mp4 in folder a, and write a/movie.ja.srt. Run PUT /api/files/{clip}/rename with {new_filename:'movie.ja.mp4'}. The rename answers 200. GET /api/files/{movie} lists no 'ja' track, and GET /api/files/{clip} lists movie.ja.srt as the bare track. I2 requires a 409 subtitle_owner_change.

bucket_proposal.reason: I2 requires a 409 for any rename or move that would change owners, and I15 requires the same for copy candidates. Neither depends on the mover having sidecars.

findings.proposed_fix: In _sidecar_carry_plan, _validate_no_duplicates and copy_file, run the destination owner-change check (as in arrival_owner_changes or the dest_index.all() loop) even when `own` is empty. In batch rename, also update the simulated stems for such steps.
